concept_name: The Resource Pulse Effect of Tang Sanzang’s Flesh
english_name: Tang Monk Flesh as Resource Pulse
ecological_definition: Resource pulse: a scarce, high-energy resource appears in abundance at a specific time and place, triggering violent fluctuations in the local ecosystem — analogous to the population booms caused by salmon runs and acorn masts in nature
core_case: Tang Sanzang’s flesh, as a scarce resource, drew demon congregations and turf wars wherever he went, violently destabilizing the local ecology

ecological_insights: Tang Sanzang’s flesh is a scarce pulse resource · it drew demon congregations wherever he went
Monster count correlates positively with pulse intensity · Lion-Camel Ridge’s 3 demons + 12 days = highest intensity
Grassroots demons act alone (White Bone Demon / Red Boy) · backed demons tend to ally (the three demons of Lion-Camel Ridge)
When resource competition is fierce, backed demons prevail (the Great Peng dominated Lion-Camel Ridge)
The ‘scarcity’ of Tang Sanzang’s flesh is the root cause of the pulse effect · if it were ‘mass-produced’ it would lose its value
